name: Nature Recovery Grant
summary: South Cambridgeshire grants for community-led nature recovery: ecological surveys by accredited professionals, or practical habitat projects such as wildflower meadows, ponds and wetlands, hedgerow and woodland management and habitat connectivity.

amount.note: Survey grants up to £2,000; nature recovery action grants up to £5,000

reporting: Survey grantees submit the survey report by an accredited professional and written next steps; project grantees submit an end of project report by May 2028.

steps: Grants Advisory Committee considers award recommendations
Lead Cabinet Member makes the final funding decision

eligibility.rule: Has a bank account that accepts online payments, a written constitution or mission statement, and a safeguarding policy
Has landowner permission for the proposed project or survey
Project on private land is publicly accessible
Ecological survey is carried out by an accredited professional
Delivery project has clear biodiversity benefits and supports the local nature recovery and council strategy priorities
Work is still to be done and is outside development-related preliminary ecological appraisal
Previous Council grantee has submitted all required reports and officers found them satisfactory
Applies for at most two projects

documents: Evidence of landowner permission and public access arrangements
Evidence of project development, options explored, and ecological soundness for delivery projects
Three cost quotes for an ecological survey
Insurance details, such as public liability cover
Cost quotes for delivery projects, if applicable

administered_by.quote: South Cambridgeshire District Council has launched a new Nature Recovery Grant Scheme

applicant_types.quote: Applications are welcomed from: Parish and town councils Community groups; sustainability and eco groups (formal or informal) Charities and non-profit organisations South Cambridgeshire schools

geography.quote: The Nature Recovery Grant Scheme supports community-led projects that restore nature, improve biodiversity, and create healthier, greener places for people and wildlife across South Cambridgeshire.

access.quote: You can apply through the form linked at the top of the page.

window.quote: Applications are open from 23 November, 2026 to 25 January, 2027.

amount.quote: Nature recovery action grants: Up to £5,000 to support projects that deliver tangible benefits for nature.

pool.quote: A total of £25,000 is available for this scheme for 2026/27.

co_finance_required.quote: The project contributes additional value and co-benefits (e.g. funding contributions or match funding; volunteer time/expertise from other sources; collaboration between organisations, and/or evidence of local and/or Member support; communication of the project to the local community).
The grant scheme has two funding streams

reporting.quote: Recipients of the ecological survey grant will need to submit: the resulting survey report (by an accredited professional) written plans detailing 'next steps'.

effort.quote: Eligible applicants can apply by filling out the Webform on the grant webpage
Applications will be assessed by a panel of Council officers against the grant criteria.
Recommendations will be considered by the Grants Advisory Committee, with final decisions made by the Lead Cabinet Member for Healthy Communities.

All projects must obtain landowner permission and other permissions as required.
Projects on privately owned land that is not publicly accessible. Projects outside of South Cambridgeshire.
Survey Route: Surveys completed by accredited professionals.
Projects must provide clear biodiversity benefits and support nature recovery priorities as set out in the Local Nature Recovery Strategy and SCDC’s Climate and Environment Strategy (2026-2030).
Preliminary Ecological Appraisals for purposes such as development. Projects with little or no biodiversity benefit. Work previously completed.

Organisations that have previously received grant funding from the Council must have submitted all required monitoring and evaluation reports relating to earlier awards, and these reports must be deemed satisfactory by Council officers, before any new grant application will be considered by the Grants Advisory Committee (GAC).
Each applicant can apply for up to two projects.

after_award.quote: completed professional ecological survey report to SCDC, and a plan outlining their ‘next steps’ based on the findings from the report. Recipients of the implementation funding will need to complete their proposed project within one year of funding allocation and submit an end-of-project report to SCDC no later than 3 months after the project is completed.
